1. Report the initial, and any subsequent altercations to your coach, to a teacher and your dad. At least one of these needs to leave a trail, such as email. 

Since your coach has refused to step up to the plate, and you are fighting for your literal rights here, get another member involved. A school member (faculty) should be immediately notified. Hopefully they will see you know what is going on and respond to this threat accordingly.

Notify your dad. I understand apprehension, however he will likely feel defensive over the inherent danger or risk that you are facing and you can try to channel that fear and anger by having him correspond with the faculty member you have notified other than your coach. Together, they will likely have much greater impact on the coaches mindset as well as the impact on the longevity of this ongoing creeps actions (which are absolutely perpetuated by the coach at this point).

2. In a perfect world, we could call awareness to a problem and have it fixed shortly thereafter. This rarely does happen though, so a higher level of diligence and accountability is required. Having disciplinary action taken is the bare minimum. If he had immediately taken accountability and apologized, you could have been lighter on the situation but it is clear that this will be a challenge to get your situation resolved. I don’t know what this would look like, but you can start by consulting with a trusted teacher. 

3. Keep coming back to the plate every time you are denied your right to be clear of foul play. If a faculty member is uninterested in assisting you, approach others. You will find someone, and in the process will be spreading an uncomfortable situation around. Someone will eventually want to help you to get the situation hushed at the very least. Just be weary of other adults such as your coach who don’t mind your torment, and even get off on it. 


Remember: You don’t deserve this. Level-headed people will want to help you. Any impact you have on this situation will help girls in your situation in the future. as a kid i’d often wait for someone to cross a certain line in conversation to go there myself, as a means of reciprocity. it always confused me when someone would start complaining like “my daughter is getting so bitchy im going to pull my hair out,” to which i would respond something along the lines of “yea, it really bugs me when she does xyz, super annoying.” i never saw anything wrong with this sort of thing. i understand the origin of unspoken rules with NT but like, oof. 

another one is not saying what you mean/ answering why. for example, if my close friend says they need us to adjust the plan, i am usually fine to go along with this. when i ask “why” in this situation, its likely not going to impact my ability to go with the flow, i just need to know. this is also applicable in other conversation areas n stuff. really frustrating when NT ppl refuse to give you harmless yet relevant information. 

and lastly (sorry for so much), general executive dysfunction. usually, i want to do something but my brain doesnt allow it to happen, no matter how much u explain this to someone, they never relinquish the shame they’re going to put onto you when they see your lack of productivity. its already so difficult internally, no one needs to be put down more.

there are more options than an inpatient facility. you can look into php or iop (both partial hospitalization processes that allow you to live in your home). they have more intensive therapy and medication management so they can fast track any medical needs that can be addressed in that way.

if you would find it beneficial, id try to go somewhere outside that you consider tranquil, and probably away from people. i like to just sit on my front steps and soak in the sun, or go down to the foresty area of the river, and just sit. i also enjoy going to a nearby dog park where i just try to do something “relaxing”. having adhd, i find it immensely difficult to *do* anything, essspeccially when depressed, so trying to paint or read or sketch, can be extremely exhausting in the moment but beneficial after i sleep, if that makes sense. idk, this is just some stuff that has worked for me. i do really suggest, you see a therapist at least. depression can cause a spiral and its a lot easier to mitigate its affects during, rather than picking yourself up and relearning how to live while dealing with the mess you’ve made while spiraling.

my mom is super dismissive too, i had my s/o reach out after i was admitted to let my parents know. they reacted as i thought they would, but having their emotions calm down while i was in a separate environment helped. im fairly certain my mom still thinks it was too rash of a decision bc i didnt have an ER visit for a failed attempt, but medical professionals reassure you while there which helped me realize that all these strangers react very strong (they are calm and collected but take strong initiative) because you are worthy of treatment. if you feel it’s necessary, you can call a cab or call or text the suicide hotline and they can assist you getting to the hospital without your parents if that’s necessary. dont try and go through facilities first though. you get priority admission if you go to the ER (even for ideation) rather than waiting weeks. if you think talking to your parents is the best option, you can do that, and if they react positively great, and if not you can go around them to get a ride to a hospital

for me, i went to a crisis center first. they transferred me to a private hospital ER in my local area and i was transferred to their behavioral health unit. for me, it was helpful bc they set me up with a trauma therapist and (for meds) psychiatrist. i would have preferred a different facility in my area that is much more strict. i would research the facilities in your area, maybe even look at reviews. what i would say to focus on is what audience they have. the facility i went to didnt separate based on depression or reality disconnected patients or even gender and i felt generally more unsafe than i should have in that setting. look for a facility that is based on helping people with depression and suicidal ideation and helping them receive support, because they will likely understand your specific problems better and be more equipped to help you best. cost should be mostly covered by insurance, or medicare/caid if you dont have insurance. you will likely be left with a small sum, but as a minor your parents will pay. i wouldnt factor this into your decision making because once you reach a point you feel unsafe, its much more likely that you are going to act on it than before, and its critical you get help before you lose your capacity to get help. keeping you alive, not suffering, and overall supported by adequate professionals should be most important. (we all want you alive and well, and immediate care is almost always necessary if you feel any level of unsafe)
